html:
The killing of West African soldiers by French troops at the Thiaroye camp near Dakar on 1 December 1944.

The men were Tirailleurs who had been prisoners of war in German camps and had just come home. They protested because they had not been paid their back pay and savings. French officers ordered troops to fire on them. The official toll was 35 dead; historians think it was much higher. For decades France hid the facts. Ousmane Sembene made the film Camp de Thiaroye (1988), which was long banned in France. In 2024 the French president formally recognised it as a massacre. See also the Second World War.
sum: The killing of West African soldiers by French troops at the Thiaroye camp near Dakar on 1 December 1944.
